messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — our nightbench run on the dedicated pool shows a steady RSS bump vs baseline (~+200MB p95). Can someone help triage? runtime image: sha=0a1b2c3, config: batch=8, seq=1024.

arjun: Can you paste the exact bench command and a pprof heap dump if available? Also which model + quantization?

maya: model: redwood/open-ggml-13b-q4_0, quant: q4_0. Command I ran:
```bash
./bench_run --model open-ggml-13b-q4_0 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --threads 4 --duration 30m
```
log snippet: RSS p95 3.2GB -> 3.4GB over ~20m, CPU steady. No spikey GC logs.

kevin: Did we switch allocator or allocator flags in the infra roll last week? I recall a change touching jemalloc params.

liz: @maya can you try a quick run with MALLOC_CONF override to see if decay settings change trend? e.g. `MALLOC_CONF=\"dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000\"` and upload heap profile.

maya: starting that run now, will attach pprof when finished.

alloc-bot: heap profile uploaded: https://internal-artifacts/pprof/1758509999/heap.pb.gz (12MB). Alloc stats: active=3.45GB, resident=3.50GB, mapped=3.70GB. Top sites: kvcache::insert, kvcache::grow_shard, slab::alloc_small.

arjun: looking at pprof quickly — lots of fragmentation from many small arena allocations (kvcache hotspot). Suggest trying a jemalloc purge in repro or adjust arena settings. Example debug call:
```c
// force purge during repro to see immediate effect
int ret = mallctl("arena.purge", NULL, NULL, NULL, 0);
```
or run with JEMALLOC_CONF to tune decay/purge.

kevin: If this is infra-related, we should bisect the infra commits touching allocator flags between 0a1b2c3 and 0f9e8d7. @maya can you run the bench against commit 0a1b2c3 (pre-change) as a control?

maya: queued a bisect job for commit 0a1b2c3 now on dedicated pool. ETA ~1.5h.

infra-bot: nightly canary deploy finishing: infra-allocator-feat at 1758510000.

liz: if bisect points to infra, patch plan: revert the allocator flag tweak to previous defaults and add jemalloc stats to /metrics for quicker detection. Also consider enabling jemalloc purge on idle to limit fragmentation.

kevin: another approach: reduce number of tiny allocations in kvcache by preallocating shard buckets or using an arena per-shard. I'll draft a PR for a prealloc bump and add instrumentation.

maya: will post bisect result + new pprof once the run completes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

arjun: one more note — if bisect shows nothing, next step is to run glibc malloc profiling and a synthetic alloc stress to reproduce deterministically. Also run with `JEMALLOC_STATS` enabled to capture per-arena fragmentation metrics.
